paper_metadata.title: Change of Mechanical Property and Fracture Mode of Molybdenum by Carbon Addition

evidence.section: Abstract
evidence.quote: Commercially available specimens of pure molybdenum were immersed in a graphite-filled Ta container and heated at a relatively low temperature of 1373 and 1473 K for 1.2 to 18.0 ks.

evidence.section: 2.1 Materials and specimen preparation
evidence.quote: The specimens were immersed in a graphite-filled Ta container. Then the container was heated to 1373 or 1473 K at a rate of 0.67 K/s in vacuum. The container was held at this temperature for 1.2 to 18.0 ks and then cooled to room temperature in a furnace.

evidence.section: 1. Introduction
evidence.quote: In fact, they observed precipitates (Mo2C) in the specimen that had been carbon-added at 1773 K or higher. A carbon content of 14 mass ppm is just the critical value for no precipitation or carbide precipitation.

evidence.section: 2.2 Three-point bending test and fracture surface observation
evidence.quote: Before carbon addition, the fracture mode is primarily of the intergranular type (indicated by ‘ ‘A’ ’ in the figure), and the specimen indicates a relatively high PIF-value.

evidence.section: 2.2 Three-point bending test and fracture surface observation
evidence.quote: After carbon addition, in contrast, the fracture mode is primarily of the transgranular type (indicated by ‘ ‘B’ ’), and the specimen indicates a relatively low PIF-value.
